title: France Has More Time Zones Than Any Other Country 🕐 #shorts
description:
France uses 12 time zones – 13 if you count its claim in Antarctica – more than any other country, even Russia and the USA with 11 each. Mainland France has just one; the rest come from overseas territories spread from UTC−10 in French Polynesia to UTC+12 in Wallis and Futuna, a 22-hour spread. And thanks to French Guiana, France's longest land border (about 730 km) is with Brazil.

Sources: Guinness World Records, timeanddate.com, Wikipedia (Time in France, Brazil–France border), CIA World Factbook, France.fr, IFLScience, Statista

scenes.text: The country with the most time zones on Earth is not Russia, and not the USA. It's France.

ZONES ON

scenes.text: France uses twelve time zones. Thirteen, if you count its claim in Antarctica.
scenes.label: TIME ZONES

scenes.text: Russia and the United States? They only have eleven each.
Mainland France has just one. The rest come from overseas islands and territories all over the world.
They stretch from ten hours behind world time in Tahiti, to twelve hours ahead in Wallis and Futuna.
That's a spread of twenty-two hours inside one country.
scenes.label: HOUR SPREAD

scenes.text: In winter, when it's lunchtime in Paris, it's one in the morning in Tahiti.
The twist? France's longest land border isn't with Spain. It's with Brazil, about seven hundred thirty kilometers through the jungle of French Guiana.
